_lane: asmopt_bf16_20260827 -- the fused BF16 GEMM task, driven from GEAK_tunerint instead of GEAK, on a two-day wall-clock budget
_why_this_file_exists: Before this file, NOTHING pointed the BF16 task at GEAK_tunerint. The three older bf16 lane files that live in this repo (coldstart_ladder_20260820, coldstart_newgate_20260819, greedy_bf16_gemm) are copies whose kernel_path / workflow_dir / state_dir all still read /home/yxh/GEAK, so launching one of them from inside GEAK_tunerint drives the OLD tree -- the paths, not the working directory, decide. The jumpbox pipeline agrees with them: geak_pipeline/config.sh has WORK_DIR=/home/yxh/GEAK and the string GEAK_tunerint appears zero times in any of its scripts. So this is the first bf16 lane whose four paths are all inside GEAK_tunerint.
_what_this_measures: The same eleven-case suite geomean against the same immutable rocBLAS oracle as the bf16 lanes in GEAK. The seed is byte-identical: `diff -rq` between GEAK/examples/tasks/dense_bf16_gemm_fused and this repo's copy reports no differing files -- only build artifacts, __pycache__, torch's hipify twins, and .orig_gfx90a_bug backups exist on the GEAK side. So the starting point is shared and the numbers are comparable to those lanes at the seed. What is NOT shared is the workflow code: this repo's kernel_lane.js, kernel_workflow.js and every role file differ from GEAK's, and this repo adds roles/asm_engineer.md, roles/update_experience.md and knowledge/learned. Read a curve from this lane against a curve from GEAK's as 'different workflow code on the same task', not as a paired control.
_note_state_dir: A new empty tunerint state directory. Older continuation state predates config-search/v2 and does not carry a canonical asm_tuner selection, so reinterpreting it would mix runtime contracts. Later waves continue this new state normally.
_note_budget: 120, not the 12 that coldstart_ladder_20260820 runs at, and for the reason fp8_rowwise_20260827 already records: budget counts dispatched engineer directions, not hours, so a budget tuned to fit two days would have to predict agent latency. Oversizing it and stopping on the wall clock puts the stop where the requirement actually is. If the lane still reports stopped_by=budget_exhausted before the deadline, that is a real finding -- the search ran out of routes, not out of time.
_note_two_days: There is NO deadline argument. The deadline subsystem (deadline_epoch / no_stop_s / max_forced_replans) was REMOVED from kernel_lane.js; those keys are not in KNOWN_ARGS and passing one is a hard error before any GPU work. GEAK's live copy of coldstart_ladder_20260820.json still carries deadline_epoch because it predates the removal -- that is one more reason not to reuse it here. 'Two days' is enforced from OUTSIDE, by kernel_workflow/scripts/lane_two_day_run.sh.
_note_candidate_floor:
0.8, and as of 2026-09-01 it means one thing: a candidate is worth measuring if it runs at least 0.8x as fast as the version we already have. kernel_lane.js computes that ratio itself, in `vsIncumbent()`, as an unweighted geomean of incumbent_ms / candidate_ms over the routes both sides reported -- the incumbent's milliseconds from THIS wave's baseline run on CANONICAL, the candidate's from its own per_case. It is NOT compared against the engineer's `speedup_geomean` any more.
That last sentence is the whole fix. `speedup_geomean` has no denominator pinned by the schema: on dense_fp8_gemm_rowwise the engineers report against the oracle (~1.19), on dense_bf16_gemm_fused's phase2 rounds against an in-session control arm (~1.003). One absolute floor was being compared against both. Set to 1.2 on 08-27 against a bf16 incumbent reading 1.5804 vs rocBLAS, it survived that lane's switch to control arms and then silently compared 1.003 against 1.2 forever -- nothing errored, because primSpeedup reads the same key either way. Counted on disk 2026-09-01: 40 patch-bearing engineer slots over seven waves, 28 of them (70%) with no verify artifacts at all, 8 of 8 in the live wave. round_4/engineer_0 carried decode_m32_down 1.0423 and prefill_m512_up 1.0151 against its own control and was never independently measured; under the new rule it scores 1.0039x the incumbent and is verified.
Comparing raw times also deletes the cold-start special case that the old hand-set floors existed for (0.29 against a 0.3353 seed, 0.37 against 0.437). At a cold start the incumbent IS the cold seed, so a candidate sitting next to it scores ~1.0 here and passes on its own. There is no longer a number to re-tune when a lane climbs.
Cross-invocation drift on an unchanged tree is 1.5-3% on this box. That is why routeGate insists on a same-session control arm; it is irrelevant to a screen carrying 20% of slack. `vsIncumbent` returns null when no route lines up and both callers treat null as PASS -- a screen that cannot see is not entitled to refuse.
Banking is untouched. COMMIT is judgeCandidate at kernel_lane.js:3907, which returns routeGate's verdict: the suite geomean must improve at all (>1.0, no threshold) AND at least one route must clear max(MIN_ROUTE_WIN=2%, that route's measured floor), minus the CATASTROPHIC_REGRESSION fence. Companion change the same day: an engineer that reports patch_file is now ALWAYS sent to verify, because a self-report is not entitled to suppress an independent measurement.
_note_no_sol_shapes: OMITTED, unlike fp8_rowwise_20260827 which passes it. This task has no sol_shapes.json: `examples/tasks/dense_bf16_gemm_fused/sol_shapes.json` does not exist, while the fp8 task's does. The consequence is real and should not be papered over -- the TechLead's stop decision rests on the geomean alone, with no roofline ceiling behind it. Generating one is the fix, but it has to be generated FROM scripts/task_runner.py:CASES and pinned by test_sol_shapes_manifest.py, because a hand-written manifest that has drifted from the suite pairs one route's bound with another route's time and produces a number that is wrong without looking wrong. Passing a path that does not exist would be worse than omitting the key.
_note_gpu_ids: 2-7, the same pool as both the fp8 lane and the bf16 lanes in GEAK. gpu_lock.sh flocks per id, so lanes sharing the pool interleave correctly instead of corrupting each other's timings. Lanes 0 and 1 are NOT usable: gpu_lock.sh opens the lock file for WRITE and /tmp/team_gpu_locks/gpu_0.lock and gpu_1.lock are root-owned, so flock fails for user yxh. That is what scripts/lockable_lanes.py records, and it is why the pool is six and not eight.
_note_isa_stays_at_observe: 'observe', not 'gate'. The ISA layer is the VERIFICATION receipt -- did the rewrite reach the binary -- and gating on it has never run for real. It is worth saying that this matters MORE in this repo than in GEAK: this tree adds roles/asm_engineer.md, so candidates here may legitimately hand-edit assembly, and a hand-edited kernel is the case most likely to read as mechanism_verdict=refuted by construction. Promote to 'gate' only after a wave of verdicts is read by hand, and only as a deliberate recorded change.
_wave_rules: examples/tasks/dense_bf16_gemm_fused/oracle_wrapper.py is the immutable oracle and the denominator of every speedup. Never edit it. Exempt it with --immutable in every candidate_policy_scan.py run.

Candidates may not link rocBLAS / hipBLAS / hipBLASLt / Tensile / Composable Kernel / MIOpen / aiter. rocWMMA is header-only and allowed. PROVENANCE.json states this ban; the oracle itself is the only thing permitted to call rocBLAS.
Do not modify baseline / harness / oracle. The workflow copies its own workspace; kernel_path itself stays untouched.

geak_tuner_runtime.py is the only dynamic-loader exception. Its hash is part of the canonical task digest and the independent verifier must pass before it may be exempted. The runtime table, generated source and selected ELF are candidate-owned and must all be scanned; no other loader is allowed.

_not_passed_on_purpose.sol_shapes: See _note_no_sol_shapes. The manifest does not exist for this task.
_not_passed_on_purpose.route_bands: Omitted. Every route is held to MIN_ROUTE_WIN (2%), judged against an incumbent re-run in the candidate's own session. There is no per-machine floor table left to pass, and lane_args.py's only resolver (@current_epoch) was deleted with it.
_not_passed_on_purpose.deadline_epoch: DOES NOT EXIST any more. Passing it is a hard error. See _note_two_days.
_not_passed_on_purpose.max_forced_replans: Removed with the deadline subsystem. Same story.
_not_passed_on_purpose.compiler_source_dir: Omitted = empty, which is what this image wants. L4 Tier 2 is an optional read-only AMDGPU checkout; this image ships no backend sources, and compiler_engineer.md is written to finish on Tier 0 (perf_knowledge/compiler_grounding/) and Tier 1 (optimization remarks) or return inconclusive.
_not_passed_on_purpose.search_strategy: REMOVED from the code. Greedy is the only strategy and the entry point throws on the key.
_not_passed_on_purpose.dra_enabled: Omitted for the first wave, matching how the fp8 lane opened. The Research phase is worth adding once a profile exists on this tree.

task: fused BF16 GEMM on MI300X; target the 11-case suite geomean against the immutable rocBLAS oracle (direct rocblas_gemm_ex). The seed sits at 0.3353 of that oracle. Forbidden in candidates: rocBLAS, hipBLAS, hipBLASLt, Tensile, Composable Kernel, MIOpen, aiter. rocWMMA is header-only and allowed. The immutable oracle is examples/tasks/dense_bf16_gemm_fused/oracle_wrapper.py -- exempt it with --immutable in every candidate_policy_scan run and never edit it. This tree carries an asm_engineer role, so assembly-level rewrites are in scope; the ISA layer is at observe, so an assembly rewrite must still be shown to have reached the binary rather than asserted.
_note_tuner_bridge: This lane is bound to the canonical asm_tuner task manifest. Every Engineer workspace runs search/create/select/materialize under gpu_lock.sh + gpu_fence_run.sh before the Engineer call; required mode fails closed. A fresh tunerint state dir avoids reinterpreting an older v1 registry or a canonical best that did not carry asm_tuner_selection.json.
_note_tuner_warm_start: Historical warm-start patches have no asm_tuner registry id and cannot be independently re-materialized. warm_start is off for this migration lane; required mode fails closed rather than timing such a patch against an unrelated/default release.
